metadata.description: Plugins. Enable only the ones that match the work in front of you.

plugins.name: engineering-strategy
plugins.description:
Write a living engineering strategy in the repo you are working in.

- engineering-strategy: When staff-plus or architecture work needs a living strategy, run explore, diagnose, refine, policy, and operations; write docs/engineering-strategy.md or docs/<slug>-engineering-strategy.md in reader order.
- strategy-explore: When you have not yet explored the problem, write the implicit rules in this repo, the alternatives, and what others already do for this kind of problem, to docs/<slug>-strategy-explore.md.
- strategy-diagnosis: When the challenge is unclear, write a theory of the problem, the dissenting views, and the data that exists, to docs/<slug>-strategy-diagnosis.md.
- strategy-refine: Before you roll a strategy out widely, pick test, map, model, both, or skip, and write docs/<slug>-strategy-refine.md.
- strategy-operations: When guiding policies already exist, write how you inspect them, the exception path, and the review cadence.
- strategy-evaluate: When a living strategy file already exists, read how fast you can iterate, what the next test costs, and whether the file still fits the diagnosis, then write docs/<slug>-strategy-evaluate.md and leave the strategy file as it is.

plugins.name: frontend-aesthetics
plugins.description:
Give a screen a specific look, not a generic layout.

- frontend-aesthetics: When you build or restyle a user interface, pick a concrete visual direction and ship production states instead of a default card grid.

plugins.name: lab
plugins.description:
Laboratory informatics for a LIMS, LIS, or ELN.

- lab-informatics-profile: When you start a LIMS, LIS, or ELN repo, or when compliance overlays are unknown, run the closed-question intake and write docs/lab-informatics-profile.md in the consuming repo.
- lab-informatics-compliance: When you design or review features that create, store, sign, or report laboratory records, load only the overlays the profile or an explicit flag turned on.
- lab-system-csv: When GAMP 5 validation of the LIMS, LIS, or ELN itself is in scope, write the category, user requirements, risk, qualification protocols, and traceability files.
- lab-part-11-review: When 21 CFR 11 or Annex 11 review is in scope, write the operational procedure for electronic records, signatures, and periodic audit-trail review.

plugins.name: lean-gate
plugins.description:
Stop at git commit and git push, and keep only the change the request actually needs.

The gate stays on until you turn it off in the project.

- lean-gate: Before you commit or push, walk the staged or to-be-pushed diff and ship the smallest change that meets the request.

plugins.name: sdd-loop
plugins.description:
Take a tracker ticket from intake through merge on a written spec.

- sdd-init: When you enable spec-driven work in this repo, write SDD Scope and Verification to docs/sdd-scope.md or the agent-instruction files, then run the health check.
- sdd-doctor: When you need to know if the loop is ready, run the read-only health check.
- sdd: Start here for help, a ticket key, intake, batch, auto, review, evolve, stop, or the specify, plan, and implement aliases.
- sdd-orchestrator: When a gated ticket needs a stage, infer the stage and run the matching playbook from intake through merge.
- sdd-clarify: When a ticket already has a spec, re-run the Clarify Loop and keep the spec body.
- sdd-analyze: When you need a cross-check of spec, design, tasks, and code, run the read-only analyze gate.
- sdd-constitution: When the project constitution needs an amendment after init, edit docs/sdd-constitution.md.
- sdd-converge: After verify, when acceptance criteria are still uncovered, run another dev pass until the ticket is Converged.
- sdd-status: When you only need a one-screen read, print the queue, inferred stage, GATES, PENDING, ATTENTION, and preflight.

plugins.name: skill-authoring
plugins.description:
Create a skill pack, or restructure one that already exists.

- skill-builder: When you create a new skill or pack, make a folder with SKILL.md, references/, and optional scripts or assets, and write the YAML description as a when-to-invoke trigger.
- skill-doctor: When an existing SKILL.md, agent-instruction file, or pack is too long or the description is only a summary, restructure it and keep the meaning.
- plugin-semver: When you change a published plugin or the marketplace catalog, bump plugin and catalog versions from the surface you added or broke.

plugins.name: software-engineering
plugins.description:
Write and change source code.

- test-driven-development: Write a failing test for the missing behavior before you write production code.
- parameterized-testing: Put every case for one behavior in one table, and give each row a name.
- systematic-debugging: Reproduce the bug before you edit.
- verification-before-completion: Run the checks on this tree and paste the command and the output before you say the work is done.
- code-simplify: Delete and flatten extra code; use the language, then a framework already in the repo, then a library already in the repo.
- requesting-code-review: Read the whole diff and write findings as file:line plus severity.
- receiving-code-review: Open the cited line, then fix it, reject it and say why, or ask if you need more.
- complexity-refactor: Measure cyclomatic complexity, then refactor the worst functions first.
- comment-police: Add no comments when writing or editing source, unless an exception applies.
- exhaustive-match: When you switch, match, or map a closed set of keys, handle every member or fail; do not hide a new key in a silent else.

plugins.name: solution-architecture
plugins.description:
Requirements and architecture for the current engagement.

- requirements-defaults: During a discovery call or before RSCOP and SAD work, walk each NFR category as HIT, MISS, DEFAULT, or ASK, and write docs/<slug>-nfr-discovery.md.
- rscop-analysis: When you have a SOW, discovery notes, or intake, write a Reliability, Security, Cost, Operations, and Performance analysis where every row has a measurable target.
- solutions-architecture-document: When an RSCOP file exists, write the Solutions Architecture Document from it and link the ADRs.
- architecture-decision-records: When a decision needs a durable record, write an ADR with status, supersedes, options, and consequences.
- c4-diagrams: When the deliverable is a C4 model, draw Context and Container, and add Deployment when asked.
- requirements: When you start a feature or new feedback arrives, draft a numbered FR-* and NFR-* spec and stop for a human sign-off.
- astro-elt-contexts: When you design, generate, or review warehouse ELT on Astro, Airflow, or dbt, land the source, transform it, and publish a contract; apply every gate before you write files.

plugins.name: writing
plugins.description:
Draft in the user's voice, and write errors they will see.

Voice stays off until you turn it on in the project.

- writing-voice: When you draft or revise documents, guides, emails, chat, tickets, or commit messages on the user's behalf, write the way this person writes.
- writing-error-messages: When you write or revise an error the user will see, say what happened, why, and what they should do next.
